scope: Manually reviewed typed constructive operations, not whole-paper operational equivalence or unspecified automation.

requirements.boundary: Except represents a typed error outcome; it is not an untyped universal bottom or divergence equivalence theorem.

Paper C3 exists as a separate typed object path. Merge selection, normalization and source-trace output have generic kernel correspondence to the certified merge. One-root batch/scalar equality holds for every graph; every successful uncached run has a recursive source-style graph trace, transferred to a cached batch by optional admission on supplied inputs. Universal graph/cache coherence remains unproved. The main C4 object path has its own policy; no policy equivalence is asserted. Checked preparation validates retained caches and freezes function/supers/order; raw overrides remain permissive. Prepared values are runtime checked data, not kernel C3 certificates.

operations: valid-record preservation and untouched-field kernel laws
requirements.boundary: These catalogs close the named typed operations. Callable carriers are statically checked and application refinements are checked; arbitrary function behavior, closure serialization and unspecified universal automation are not established. Prepared JSON codecs cover finite catalogs with unique nonempty labels and codecs on every field. Descriptor APIs admit refinements; the raw codec layer is unchecked. No generic codec inverse theorem or textual duplicate-key rejection is claimed. Heterogeneous patch is supported with explicit declaration/refinement premises and kernel validity/frame laws.
Runtime capability consumption is enforced, including concurrent consumers. No static ownership calculus, generic effectful rollback or universal pure/mutable isomorphism theorem is claimed.

Lean uses the shared thunk implementation for the internal-define/letrec/lazy routes. Direct untyped Y self-application is a language choice; rebuilding behavior is tested, not a universal Y equivalence or termination theorem. The finite iteration API certifies a fixed point when adjacent approximations are proved equal. General shared-thunk equivalence remains unproved.
